To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the application of biomarker approaches to monitor aquatic ecosystems has increased in recent decades, 2) Mediterranean rivers have unique characteristics that should be taken into account when selecting the most appropriate biomarkers to assess the status of these ecosystems, 3) the use of biomarker approaches in the context of the Water Frame Directive is still scarce in Mediterranean rivers but has increased in the last years, 4) multi biomarker approaches are more sensitive to detect early signs of stress than single biomarkers

(a) the application of biomarker tools is increasing in European rivers and the Mediterranean basin, but there is still a long way to go; (b) there is a need for a more harmonised approach, especially regarding the use of sentinel species and the design of biomarker studies; and (c) the application of a multi biomarker approach is essential to better understand the causes and effects, and to predict the responses to stressors of the Mediterranean biodiversity.

the use of biomarkers in Mediterranean rivers can be improved by considering the ecological traits of the species, the structure of the food webs and the environmental context of the study, in order to increase the ecological relevance and the applicability of biomarkers to the management and conservation of Mediterranean fluvial ecosystems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effects of human activities on the structure of aquatic ecosystems and their functioning.
the study of aquatic ecosystems and their response to human impacts.
the development of a multi biomarker approach for the assessment of the health status of aquatic ecosystems, with a focus on the ecological relevance of the responses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
biomarkers can be used as a valuable and cost-effective tool to detect and quantify the effects of multiple stressors on the health status of riverine communities.
biomarker studies have a high potential to provide a better understanding of the causes of biodiversity loss and its implications for ecosystem services in Mediterranean rivers.
biomarkers are a useful tool in the assessment of the ecological status of Mediterranean rivers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
biomarkers are a valuable tool for the assessment of the health status of Mediterranean rivers and their communities, and that their use should be increased and improved in the near future.

biomarkers can provide a more comprehensive assessment of the health status of riverine ecosystems, and that they should be used to complement other standardised procedures of environmental assessment.

biomarkers can provide a more holistic view on the health of aquatic communities, and that they should be incorporated in monitoring programmes to better appraise and protect biodiversity in Mediterranean rivers.
The main takeaway from our work is that

biomarker studies should not be restricted to a single species, but instead should include a multi species approach, in which the responses of the sentinel species are interpreted within the context of their role and position in the ecosystem.
the application of biomarker responses should be considered as a key tool to assess the health of aquatic ecosystems and the effects of stressors, including the ones related to climate change.

the use of multi biomarker approaches is a cost effective tool to assess and manage anthropogenic impacts in Mediterranean rivers, and that the use of biomarkers in the assessment of river health is an essential component in the implementation of the Water Frame Directive.
